construct: PMM2 encodes phosphomannomutase 2, which converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate. Loss of PMM2 lowers the mannose-1-phosphate/GDP-mannose pool and impairs synthesis of lipid-linked oligosaccharides required for N-linked protein glycosylation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The characteristic PMM2-CDG infant phenotype plus biallelic PMM2 variants and abnormal transferrin glycoforms identifies deficient phosphomannomutase 2, which converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate for N-linked glycosylation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Mannose-6-phosphate lysosomal tagging, aldolase B, GALT, and G6PD are distinct pathways and do not account for PMM2-dependent glycosylation failure.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The gene and reaction are directly linked; none of the alternatives is catalyzed by PMM2.
